decisions.name: InMemoryAssignsAutoIncrementId
decisions.what: runPlayersInMemory's UpsertPlayerByExternalId uses an internal nextId counter (Int starting at 1)
why: Mirrors the DB's BIGSERIAL behaviour without needing an actual sequence.
Counter is per-IORef (per-runner-instance), so two concurrent test runs don't share ids.

upsertPlayerByExternalId: Players send-only; same semantics as DB upsertByExternalId
getActivePlayers: Players send-only; all players where active=True
runPlayersDB: requires Error DBError post Phase A.3
runPlayersInMemory: UpsertPlayerByExternalId: if (provider, externalId) found, update rowsByDb keeping the existing id; else assign nextId and insert into both maps
GetActivePlayers iterates all rows and filters by playerRowActive

decisions.name: MirrorsPlayersInMemoryShape
decisions.what: TeamStore has the same external-id-map + db-rows-map + nextId-counter shape as PlayerStore
why: Same trade-offs as Players: per-runner counter mimicking BIGSERIAL, no FK enforcement.
Code duplication is acceptable at two test interpreters.

runTeamsDB: requires Error DBError post Phase A.3

decisions.name: GameStoreHasReverseLookupMap
decisions.what: The in-memory game store maintains both an external-id->db-id map AND a db-id->external-id map
why: GetGameExternalId requires reverse lookup; iterating the forward map with elem-on-value would be O(n) per call.
Two maps cost twice the memory but make every lookup O(log n).

getGamesByDateRange: Games send-only; range listing inclusive on both ends
consumed by Pelotero.Score.collectGameIds to enumerate the games in the scoring period

getAll: consumed by Pelotero.Lineup.Snapshot.snapshotLineupsForGame to enumerate active leagues
runLeagueConfigDB: requires Error DBError post Phase A.3

decisions.name: NewEffectForPhaseB3
decisions.what: LineupSnapshot is a separate effect from LineupSlot; the two have different lifecycles and different consumers
why: LineupSlot is the live, mutable, owner-edited lineup. LineupSnapshot is the immutable per-game freeze. Different concerns, different effects.
Pelotero.Score reads ONLY from LineupSnapshot; Pelotero.Lineup.Snapshot writes ONLY to LineupSnapshot. Pelotero.UI / lineup management reads/writes LineupSlot.
Splitting the effects keeps the producer/consumer graph clean and avoids the temptation to read from the live lineup at scoring time (which was the original correctness bug).

writeSnapshots: LineupSnapshot send-only; writes a list of LineupSnapshotRow with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; returns ()
getSnapshotsForGame: audit/inspection use; not on the scoring path

getRankingsForTeam: intended consumer is the planned Pelotero.Draft state machine (D.1); no consumer in tree today

recordPick: intended consumer is the planned Pelotero.Draft state machine (D.1); no consumer in tree today
runDraftPickDB: no in-memory interpreter — draft picks are append-only and the in-memory equivalent would be a list

getBattingForGame: consumed by Pelotero.Score.buildPlayerMaps (one call per game in the period)
runBoxscoreEntryNever: test interpreter that errors on every operation
useful for tests that need BoxscoreEntry in the effect stack but exercise paths where no batting/pitching upsert should occur (e.g. C.1 SHA-skip tests with empty boxscore JSON)
any actual invocation is the test's bug, not a real failure mode — the error message names the operation that was unexpectedly called

decisions.name: UpstreamAndSurrogateAreDistinctTypes
decisions.what: PlayerId / TeamId / GameId (upstream MLB ids) and DbPlayerId / DbTeamId / DbGameId (surrogate DB BIGSERIAL ids) are different newtypes
why: Conflating them led to bugs: a function expecting an MLB id received a DB surrogate, the SQL succeeded with the wrong row, and nothing complained.
Newtype distinctness forces the conversion to be explicit (a lookup against player_external_id) rather than a coerce.
The cost is more wrappers; the win is the type system catching crossings of the layer boundary.

decisions.name: TextIdsForUserSpaces
decisions.what: LeagueId and FantasyTeamId wrap Text, not Int
why: Leagues and fantasy teams have user-chosen identifiers (e.g. 'east-coast-2025', 'rocketeers'), not auto-incremented numbers.
Database surrogate keys (DbLeagueConfigId, DbLeagueTeamId) are still Int64 for indexing efficiency; user-facing stays Text.

decisions.name: NoSmartConstructorsHere
decisions.what: All newtypes have public constructors and accessors; no smart-constructor validation
why: Validation (rejecting nonsense like PlayerId 0) happens at the wire boundary in Pelotero.MLB.Convert.convertPlayer.
The wire layer is the single source of truth for what counts as a valid id; this module is structural only.
Pelotero.Provider.ExternalId provides the to/from Text encodings (Phase A.1) but does not validate id ranges.

decisions.name: ExhaustiveSumNoCatchAll
decisions.what: The Position type is an exhaustive sum of MLB's ten positions; parsePosition returns Nothing on anything else
why: Positions are a small, stable set defined by MLB rules.
An 'Other Text' fallback constructor would make the type infectious.
Errors at the wire boundary surface as warnings, not silent fallbacks.

decisions.name: TwoWayPlayerNotModelled
decisions.what: MLB's 'TWP' (two-way player, e.g. Ohtani) is intentionally not parsed
why: TWP requires a richer domain model (a player has multiple primary positions with separate stat lines).
Out of scope for the current engine; would change scoring shape.

parsePosition: accepts BOTH MLB numeric codes ('1','2',...,'10') AND scorer abbreviations ('P','C','1B','2B','3B','SS','LF','CF','RF','DH')
isPitcher: True for Pitcher only; False for everything else including DH
isInfielder: True for FirstBase, SecondBase, ThirdBase, Shortstop, AND Catcher
Catcher being an infielder is conventional for fantasy classification
isOutfielder: DH is not an outfielder despite the position number 10 being adjacent

decisions.name: TotalHandChar
decisions.what: handChar :: Handedness -> Char is exhaustive case-of, total at the type level
why: Phase A.6 introduced this to replace the partial T.head . renderHandedness path.

Adding a new Handedness constructor is a -Wincomplete-patterns error here; the previous design (T.head over a Text) deferred totality to the renderHandedness exhaustivity, with a hidden coupling that wasn't enforced by anything visible at the call site.
The DB column for bat_side / pitch_hand remains Text (PostgreSQL CHAR(1) padding gotchas), but the API is now total Char end-to-end.

renderHandedness: kept for symmetry with parseHandedness; sync code now uses handChar instead
handChar: total; consumed by Pelotero.Sync.Players.upsertAllPlayers (replacing T.head . renderHandedness)

decisions.name: MaybeIntPerField
decisions.what: Every stat field in the per-game stats records is Maybe Int rather than Int with a default of 0
why: Distinguishes 'didn't bat' from 'batted, went 0-for-0'.
A pitcher's batting line in the AL legitimately has Nothing for atBats, not 0.
Scoring layer applies fromMaybe 0 at the point of multiplication; presence/absence info is preserved up to that point.

decisions.name: PitOutsIsCanonicalNoTextField
decisions.what: PitchingStats has pitOuts :: Maybe Int and NO pitInningsPitched field; the wire-format string is parsed at Convert time and discarded
why: Phase B.1 collapsed the redundancy. The wire ships both pitOuts (Maybe Int) and pitInningsPitched (Maybe Text); convertPitching reconciles the two and emits a WireFieldDiscrepancy warning if they disagree, then keeps only the Int.
Outs are exact integers; the Text representation was only ever a wire-layer artifact. Domain code now never has to worry about the parse round-trip footgun.
renderInningsPitched still exists for human-facing display (e.g. 'Roberts pitched 6.2 innings') but is no longer in the scoring/storage path.

emptyBatting: all-Nothing default for every BattingStats field
BattingStats has 25 Maybe Int fields; all wire-derived
emptyPitching: PitchingStats has ~40 Maybe Int fields plus pitOuts as Maybe Int (NO pitInningsPitched, post Phase B.1)
parseInningsPitched: the fractional part must be 0, 1, or 2; '6.3' returns Nothing
negative whole or fractional parts return Nothing
consumed only by Pelotero.MLB.Convert.convertPitching at the wire boundary
renderInningsPitched: kept for human-facing display only; not used in the scoring/storage path post Phase B.1

decisions.name: SeqForOrderedSlotMembers
decisions.what: Roster and Lineup both use Map RosterSlot (Seq PlayerId) — Seq, not List or Set
why: Order matters within a slot.
Set would lose ordering; List has O(n) appends; Seq has O(log n).
The slot order itself doesn't matter (Map handles that), but the order within a slot does. Persistence of within-slot order via order_index columns is planned B.2 work.

decisions.name: ValidationProducesAllErrorsNotJustFirst
decisions.what: validateRoster and validateLineup return [RosterError] / [LineupError] — all problems, not just the first
why: When showing errors in a UI, displaying 'too many at OF (3 vs 2)' AND 'duplicate player X' is more useful than 'too many at OF, retry'.
Order is: all size problems then all duplicate problems.

allRosterSlots: [minBound .. maxBound]; the canonical traversal order is the constructor order in RosterSlot
parseRosterSlot: the s_pitcher / r_pitcher names match legacy DB schema
isBatterSlot: = not . isPitcherSlot; SlotUtility is a batter slot
emptyRoster: every slot present with empty Seq
rosterAt: returns Seq.empty if the slot is somehow missing from the map
addToRoster: appends to the slot's Seq using Map.insertWith
no validation against limits at this point
removeFromRoster: removes the FIRST occurrence of pid from the slot's Seq
does nothing if the slot or pid is absent
rosterLimitFor: Map lookup; defaults to 0 if the slot has no entry
validateRoster: produces all over-limit errors then all duplicate errors
duplicates detected via group . sort, so the resulting list is in PlayerId order
validateLineup: mirror of validateRoster but with LineupError variants
duplicates: private; group . sort then take first of each group of size >= 2

decisions.name: PointsAsRationalNotDouble
decisions.what: The Points newtype wraps Rational, not Double
why: Sums of fantasy points across many games accumulate; floating drift is observable when a season total visibly disagrees with the sum of game lines.
Scaling by Rational multipliers (e.g. 1/3 for innings) stays exact end-to-end.

decisions.name: MultiplierFieldsAsExplicitRecord
decisions.what: The batting and pitching multiplier records list every scored stat as a named field
why: A Map String Rational would defer typo detection to runtime.
Adding a stat is a structural change on purpose.

decisions.name: DerivedStatsInScoringNotData
decisions.what: Singles (batting) and quality starts (pitching) are derived inside scoreBatting / scorePitching, not stored as fields
why: Singles = hits - (doubles + triples + homeRuns); the wire layer doesn't ship singles separately.
Quality start = IP >= 6 AND ER <= 3; not a stat the boxscore reports.

decisions.name: ScorePitchingReadsPitOutsDirectly
decisions.what: scorePitching reads pitOuts straight from PitchingStats; no parseInningsPitched . pitInningsPitched step (post Phase B.1)
why: The redundancy between pitInningsPitched (Maybe Text) and pitOuts (Maybe Int) is gone at the Domain level; PitchingStats now has only pitOuts.

Removes a parse step from every scoring call. More importantly, removes a class of bug where a future caller could set pitOuts without setting pitInningsPitched (or vice versa) and silently get the wrong answer.

decisions.name: InningsPitchedExactRationalArithmetic
decisions.what: scorePitching computes 'pmInningPitched * (outs / 3)' as Rational, not as a Double or pre-rounded decimal
why: Per-inning multipliers are typically integers or simple fractions; fractional outs need exact division.
Pre-rounding loses ~0.05 points per fractional inning, compounding over 150 starts.

subPoints: pointwise Rational subtraction; can produce negative Points
currently has no in-tree caller; effectively dead code retained for symmetry
scalePoints: multiplies Points by a Rational; preserves exactness
sumPoints: left-fold over a Foldable; uses zeroPoints as the seed
scoreBatting: sums per-stat contributions; each contribution is multiplier * count
singles are derived: max 0 of (hits - doubles - triples - homeRuns)
missing stats default to 0 via fromMaybe; an empty BattingStats produces zeroPoints
scorePitching: outs read directly from pitOuts (post Phase B.1); no parseInningsPitched step
qualityStarts is 1 if outs >= 18 (6 innings) AND earnedRuns <= 3, else 0
innings-pitched contribution uses Rational (outs/3) for exactness

decisions.name: PureOrderGenerator
decisions.what: generateDraftOrder is pure (no IO, no Random); randomness is supplied by the caller as the order of the input team list
why: Pure functions are testable without any randomness effect.
If the caller wants random ordering (a coin flip for first pick), they shuffle the team list outside this module and pass it in.
Keeps this module free of effects.

decisions.name: TruncateTrailingPartialRound
decisions.what: If totalPicks is not a multiple of length teams, the trailing partial round is dropped, NOT half-completed
why: A draft with N teams should always have a multiple-of-N pick count.
Half-completing a round would create asymmetry; truncating preserves the 'teams are equal' invariant.

decisions.name: PureModuleByDesign
decisions.what: This module stays pure; no effectful state machine lives here today, and a future Pelotero.Draft (planned D.1 work) will be the home of the live draft state machine when it lands
why: generateDraftOrder is pre-computation pure logic. Running an actual draft requires database writes per pick, which means the live state machine has to live in a module with effect access.
Splitting the modules keeps Pelotero.Domain.Draft testable without effects; Pelotero.Draft (when implemented) will be testable via the in-memory effect interpreters.

generateDraftOrder.intent: Produce the full pick-by-pick order as (team, pickNumber)
notes: empty teams returns []
rounds = totalPicks `div` length teams; trailing partial round is truncated
pick numbers are 1-indexed
pure: no randomness, no IO

decisions.name: LeagueStatusOnlyMutableField
decisions.what: League's only field that changes after creation is leagueStatus; everything else is the immutable league definition
why: Scoring rules, roster limits, and draft params shouldn't change mid-season.
Status moves through draft -> active -> closed in the lifecycle.

decisions.name: ScoringPeriodAsUtcTime
decisions.what: ScoringPeriod uses UTCTime, not Day
why: Real leagues have lineup-lock cutoffs at specific game start times in specific timezones.
Day would be ambiguous; UTCTime forces an explicit instant.
